title: Voice AI: when is the "Her" moment? — Neil Zeghidour, CEO, Gradium AI
talk_summary: A voice-AI model CEO argues cascaded speech pipelines still beat end-to-end speech-to-speech on reliability, tool use, and observability, and that the real bottleneck has shifted from TTS latency to unpredictable tool-call latency. He proposes filler/backchannel utterances to mask tool-call waits and on-device small TTS to control cost and privacy.

takeaways.technique: Filler output while awaiting slow tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: The LLM splits its turn: it emits a tool call and simultaneously produces a short natural filler ('Tokyo is such an incredible choice...') so the user isn't left in silence, then weaves the tool result back in when it arrives.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it sends a tool call. And while it waits for getting the result back, it can keep the conversation going in a natural way
takeaways.numbers: tool-call latency cited as 500ms–4s vs TTS ~200ms

takeaways.technique: Route by bottleneck, not by headline metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues optimizing TTS latency by 10–20ms is pointless when the tool call dominates at 500ms–4s; effort should go to the unpredictable component.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are fighting for latency of the TTS, trying to grab 10 milliseconds, 20 milliseconds, and then you have a tool call

takeaways.technique: Small local model for the high-volume cheap part
takeaways.what_they_do: Ships a <100M-parameter TTS that runs on a smartphone CPU so consumer apps pay zero API fees for the most cost-dominant component.

takeaways.technique: Keep the observable, tool-using pipeline over the opaque end-to-end one
takeaways.what_they_do: Rejects replacing the cascaded STT→LLM→TTS stack with a single speech-to-speech model because the latter has no tool calls, no observability, and no way to detect bad outputs — despite sounding more natural.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's impossible to use in production something that is as no observability

takeaways.technique: Train/eval for the signal you actually want, not just factual QA
takeaways.what_they_do: Notes speech-to-speech models carry paralinguistic information but never use it because they're trained on audio versions of factual instruct data; the capability exists but is unexploited without targeted training.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you train it on the audio version of a instruct data set ... why would it even try to capture this information?
